requirements.title: Conditional admission and transfer rules
requirements.summary: SCS entrants declare a major in first-year spring. Internal SCS transfers depend on interest, ability and space after consultation; no grade cutoff is specified. Transfers from other CMU schools or dual-degree applicants must complete 15-122, 15-150, 07-280, 07-380, one of 15-210/15-213/15-251, and one of 15-259/21-325/21-425/36-218/36-225; expected QPA across these six is at least 3.6 and overall QPA at least 3.0. Starting Fall 2026, apply to a specific major only once. Deadlines are last classes of mini-1, mini-3 or mini-6; review includes coursework, computing involvement and an essay. External university transfers apply through Admissions; admission depends on space and preparation. Admitted external transfers must remain in their initial SCS major at least one year and meet the internal transfer criteria before changing, excluding transferred courses.

requirements.title: Graduation and residence
requirements.summary: Complete the degree program with cumulative CMU QPA at least 2.00, SCS faculty recommendation, and fulfilled university financial obligations. Residence requires at least four full-time semesters or equivalent part-time study at CMU, comprising at least 180 units.

requirements.title: Good academic standing
requirements.summary: Maintain semester and cumulative QPA at least 2.00. Complete attempted foundational courses by the end of sophomore year, in at most two attempts each: C or better in 15-112, 15-122 and 15-151 (or 21-127), and D or better in 21-120 and 21-122.

requirements.title: AI-specific academic progress
requirements.summary: Complete 07-280 and the required probability course with C or better by the end of sophomore year. Complete at least one of 15-210, 15-213 or 15-251 with D or better by the end of junior year. Major-specific progress courses allow at most two attempts each. Academic-action procedures apply when good-standing conditions are unmet.

requirements.title: Current science approval rules
requirements.summary: Current science rules supplement the catalog: consult an SCS adviser before registration for every selected course; minis need adviser/associate-dean review. ECE graduate courses (18-6xx through 18-9xx) are excluded. Unlisted Engineering & Public Policy courses require adviser/associate-dean suitability review. SCS crosslists or substantial mathematical/computational content generally disqualify a course.

requirements.title: Current humanities approval rules
requirements.summary: Current humanities rules permit two minis totaling at least nine units to fulfill one breadth category only with associate-dean permission and suitable category goals. Lower-unit humanities/arts courses may combine into one nine-unit elective with adviser and associate-dean approval. AI uses Category 1A; other Category 1 options are excluded from this AI inventory.

requirements.title: Grading and repeated credit
requirements.summary: Pass/no-pass may be elected for a free elective unless disallowed; A–D earns P credit without QPA points. Audit earns no credit. Repeated-course grades all affect QPA, but units count once; repeating a passed course needs dean/department-head approval. Course prerequisites and corequisites must be met.

requirements.title: Transfer and examination credit
requirements.summary: Transfer credit needs official final transcripts, departmental equivalency/application review, and C− or better (including pass marks certified equivalent). No transfer math below Calculus I, English-language courses, career-preparation/first-year seminars or algebra-based physics. AP/IB credit applies only with home-unit approval; IB credit is restricted to Higher Level exams. Approved non-equivalent courses may count as electives or breadth where appropriate.

requirements.title: University graduation QPA exception
requirements.summary: University graduation rules allow a post-first-year QPA of at least 2.0 when a first-year entrant’s first-year grades alone cause cumulative QPA below 2.0. The transcript retains all grades; additional program QPA rules may apply, so SCS adviser confirmation is needed.

requirements.title: Certification, catalog and time limits
requirements.summary: Use applicable matriculation-catalog requirements and any approved College Council modifications. Standard study is eight semesters; earlier or longer completion is certified on meeting primary-degree requirements with adviser consultation. All degree units must be earned within eight years of award unless the dean grants a course-specific, time-bounded waiver based on currency, preparation and legitimate delay.

requirements.title: University residence and diploma conditions
requirements.summary: At least four full-time semesters or part-time equivalent and 180 units must be completed at CMU; exceptions require the home dean. Residence/course requirements, applicable QPA and financial obligations must be satisfied. These overlap the SCS graduation policy rather than adding units.

requirements.title: Optional honors thesis application
requirements.summary: Optional program: an SCS faculty adviser endorses a three-to-four-page prospectus describing the problem, significance, research plan/timeline and bibliography, with short abstract and adviser signature/email. Submit by senior-year start; junior-year submission is encouraged. There is no fixed QPA admission cutoff; 3.5 in relevant core topics is an expectation for success.

requirements.title: Optional honors thesis deliverables
requirements.summary: Normally 36 units over senior year (18 each semester), with a prior-work/progress paper, December poster, year-end poster and oral presentation, and written thesis. Optional 07-300 (9 units) and 07-400 practicum (12 units) prepare for research; practicum units may count toward the 36 thesis units when beginning that thesis. The major limits how thesis units fill electives.

requirements.title: Degree unit minimum
requirements.summary: The published degree summary requires 360 total units. Distribution totals are components of this total, not additional units.

requirements.title: Conditional eligibility for the Statistics sequence
requirements.summary: The 36-235/236 option is subject to course eligibility, not unrestricted BSAI enrollment: 36-235 requires Statistics major/minor status, sophomore standing and no prior credit in 36-217/218/219/700, 21-325 or 15-259. Consult Statistics advisers for the declaration deadline. 36-236 requires 36-235 with C or better and allows Statistics majors/minors or CS majors taking both courses; whether its CS-major exception includes BSAI is not defined. A declared Statistics-minor route is available under the university’s general minor-access rule; the minor separately requires at least three Statistics courses not counted toward the primary major. This optional minor adds its own requirements and is not required by the AI degree.

outcomes.text: Frame real-world challenges as AI problems involving models, reasoning, decisions and human interaction.
Build and analyze AI and machine-learning methods for visual, language and uncertain data.
Apply computer-science and mathematical foundations, including algorithms, probability and optimization.
Develop substantial AI systems, communicate technical ideas and collaborate effectively.
Assess ethical, legal, privacy and broader societal consequences of AI.
